meta.title: ai-scan-orientation · LRO Front, Worker, Python Compute
meta.subtitle: MLE · system moa · the canonical postgres-lro service shape

views.label: Submit and poll
views.note: Callers use Compute, GetOperation and WaitOperation on port 50051. WaitOperation is capped at 10 minutes.

views.label: Claim and compute
views.note: The worker claims one row, keeps the lease alive, then calls the Python sidecar over localhost:50071.

views.label: Inside the worker pod
views.note: Two containers share one pod. Blob IDs become signed URLs because the Python side has no storage credentials.

cards.title: The LRO front is twenty lines
items: main.go only supplies serviceName, validateRequest and a whitelist
Queue mechanics, the Operations API and the Deployment come from the shared spine
The Deployment itself is contributed by k8s/postgres-lro-patch/lro

cards.title: Worker to sidecar
items: Cold start is slow, so the call is retried 15 times at 1s intervals
Only codes.Unavailable is retried; any other error fails the item immediately
The response is marshalled through Any to cross the proto namespace boundary

cards.title: Why the sidecar is the heavy box
items: Go container limits are 1 CPU and 1024Mi; the Python container gets 5 CPU and 10Gi
Both land on the MLE node pool via nodeType=mle:NoSchedule toleration
Datadog tags the sidecar logs with source python, so it shows up as its own service

cards.title: Operations
items: LRO duration threshold is 30s under opdoc MOA-001; the worker is MOA-002
Backstage fans this out into service, dbmigrations, smoketest and api components
